apo_histha.text:
Oṁ āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvaḥ
tā na ūrje dadhātana
mahe raṇāya cakṣase

yo vaḥ śivatamo rasaḥ
tasya bhājayateha naḥ
uśatīr iva mātaraḥ

tasmā araṁ gamāma vaḥ
yasya kṣayāya jinvatha
āpo janayathā ca naḥ

lines.meaning: Oṁ. Waters, you are indeed bringers of well-being.
As such, grant us nourishment and strength.
For great, delightful vision/perception.

words.meaning: for great; qualifying the requested vision/perception
for delight; taken with cakṣase as delightful vision/perception

lines.meaning: That essence of yours which is most auspicious—
Let us share in that essence here.
Like loving mothers.
For that, may we readily approach you—

words.meaning: for that one/that aim (tasmai in Vedic vowel sandhi)

lines.meaning: For whose dwelling you give vitality.
Waters, also bring us into renewed life.

readingNotes: This is the first three verses of Ṛgveda 10.9, arranged as three groups of three phrases. Vedic accent is not supplied.
ṣṭhā represents the recited sandhi hi + stha; do not silently change it to Classical Sanskrit sthā.

mahe raṇāya cakṣase is understood together as “for great, delightful vision/perception,” continuing the request to the waters for strength; the words are not three unrelated ritual requests. The syntax of tasmā ... yasya is disputed: the last verse can be understood as approaching the waters for the one whose dwelling they enliven. kṣaya here means dwelling/abode; no unsupported gloss “destruction of sins” is inserted. janayathā literally asks the waters to generate us, rendered as renewal of life.
Primary textual comparison: https://lrc.la.utexas.edu/books/rigveda/RV10 (10.009.01–03).

corrections.reason: Joins the compound mayaḥ + bhuvaḥ and normalizes the visarga.
Separates the two Vedic words; no text is added.
Separates tasya; bhājayateha retains bhājayata + iha sandhi.
Separates iva while preserving the sandhi r.
Corrects the printed long vowel after y to the Rigvedic janayathā; final ā is retained.

lines.meaning: Oṁ. Reverence to Nārāyaṇa. Oṁ.

readingNotes: The source directs twelve repetitions while touching the vehicle or implement. The two printed Oṁ syllables are retained.

deity_salutations.text:
sarvebhyo devebhyo namaḥ
sarvebhyo tattvābhimānibhyo devebhyo namaḥ
tattvanāsikā devatābhyo namaḥ
mātṛkānyāsa devatābhyo namaḥ

lines.meaning: Reverence to all the deities.
Reverence to all the deities presiding over the principles of existence.

words.meaning: to the presiders over principles of existence (tattva + abhimānin; plural dative in sandhi)

lines.meaning: Reverence to the deities designated by tattvanāsikā; literally “principle + nose,” its intended deity class is not securely identifiable.

words.meaning: tattva (principle of existence) + nāsikā (nose); intended deity class not securely identifiable

lines.meaning: Reverence to the deities of mātṛkā-nyāsa, the ritual placement of sacred letters.

readingNotes: The malformed printed tattvābhimāninai is corrected to the plural dative tattvābhimānibhyo, agreeing with sarvebhyo and devebhyo. This is a grammatical correction, not an addition of a deity class.

tattvanāsikā is retained exactly, not replaced with conjectural tattvanyāsikā. Its components literally mean principle + nose, but the intended deity class is not securely identifiable; it cannot safely be glossed as nyāsa (ritual placement).

corrections.reason: Normalizes the Sanskrit consonant doubling in tattva. The malformed ending is corrected separately below.
Corrects the malformed dative ending to the plural dative of tattvābhimānin, agreeing with sarvebhyo devebhyo; before d, final -bhyaḥ becomes -bhyo.

ayudha_prayer.text:
sarvāyudhānāṁ prathamaṁ nirmitāsi pinākinā
śūlāyudhād viniṣkṛṣya kṛtvā muṣṭigrahaṁ śubhaṁ
churike rakṣa māṁ nityaṁ śāntiṁ yaccha namo’stu te

lines.meaning: You were fashioned first among all weapons by Pinākin, Śiva.

words.meaning: by Pinākin, the bearer of the Pināka bow

lines.meaning: Having drawn [you] out from the spear weapon and made an auspicious handgrip—

words.meaning: from the spear weapon (śūla + āyudha; ablative)

lines.text: churike rakṣa māṁ nityaṁ śāntiṁ yaccha namo’stu te
lines.meaning: O dagger, protect me always; grant peace. Reverence be to you.

readingNotes: This prayer addresses a churikā, a dagger or knife, as a feminine deity. Its literal wording is not a universal prayer to a computer or every tool.

The middle line is corrected using Kamalākara Bhaṭṭa’s Śūdrakamalākara, which quotes Viṣṇudharma: https://vishvasa.github.io/kalpAntaram/dharmaH/nibandhaH/shUdra-dharmaH/shUdra-kamalAkaraH/mUlam/ . The witness contains additional stanzas absent from the selected source; these are not added.
The subject of nirmitāsi is the feminine churikā addressed in the final line.

corrections.reason: Separates the imperative and its object.
Marks the elided initial a of astu; pronunciation is unchanged.
Independent Śūdrakamalākara witness reads शूलायुधाद् विनिष्कृष्य; replaces the damaged case ending and participle without adding omitted stanzas.

kalasha_prayer.text:
devadānavasaṁvāde mathyamāne mahodadhau
utpanno’si tadā kumbha vidhṛto viṣṇunā svayaṁ
tvayi tiṣṭhanti bhūtāni tvayi prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
tvatprasādāt imaṁ yajñaṁ kartumīhe jalodbhava

lines.meaning: At the encounter of gods and dānavas, while the great ocean was being churned—

words.meaning: at the encounter of gods and dānavas (deva + dānava + saṁvāda)

lines.text: utpanno’si tadā kumbha vidhṛto viṣṇunā svayaṁ
lines.meaning: O pot, you arose then and were held by Viṣṇu himself.

lines.text: tvayi tiṣṭhanti bhūtāni tvayi prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
lines.meaning: In you dwell the beings/elements; in you the vital breaths are established.
Through your favor I desire to perform this sacrifice, O water-born one.

readingNotes: Three damaged readings are corrected against an independent Sanskrit witness, Saṁskāraratnamālā, printed page 151: https://sa.wikisource.org/wiki/पृष्ठम्:संस्काररत्नमाला_(भागः_१).djvu/१५५ . Only the four source-selected lines are included; no additional stanzas are supplied.
kartumīhe joins kartum (to perform) and īhe (I desire/endeavor), not kartum + ihe.
The source allows water from the previously worshipped kalasha or worship of a new kalasha.

corrections.reason: Marks the elided a in asi.
Normalizes the clear verb “dwell/stand” by restoring aspiration.
Normalizes the clear participle “established” by restoring aspiration.
Saṁskāraratnamālā printed p.151 reads मथ्यमाने; locative participle agrees with mahodadhau.
Saṁskāraratnamālā printed p.151 reads विष्णुना स्वयम्; instrumental identifies who held the pot.
Saṁskāraratnamālā printed p.151 reads कर्तुमीहे, kartum + īhe.

upacara_list.text:
dhyāna āvāhana āsana arghya pādya ācamana
madhuparkaṁ punarācamanaṁ snānaṁ vastraṁ upavītaṁ gandhaṁ
ābharaṇāni akṣata dhūpaṁ dīpaṁ naivedyaṁ samarpayāmi

lines.text: dhyāna āvāhana āsana arghya pādya ācamana
lines.meaning: Meditation, invocation, a seat, an honorific water offering, water for the feet, and water for sipping.

lines.text: madhuparkaṁ punarācamanaṁ snānaṁ vastraṁ upavītaṁ gandhaṁ
lines.meaning: Madhuparka, water for sipping again, bathing, clothing, a sacred thread, and sandal paste/fragrance.

lines.text: ābharaṇāni akṣata dhūpaṁ dīpaṁ naivedyaṁ samarpayāmi
lines.meaning: I offer ornaments, unbroken rice, incense, a lamp, and food.

readingNotes: This preserves the source’s shortened noun list and its single final samarpayāmi. It does not supply sixteen individual offering formulas.
Several nouns appear as list labels rather than uniformly inflected accusatives. The heading calls this ṣoḍaśopacāra, but the printed enumeration has seventeen named items; do not silently omit one.

completion.text:
yasya smṛtyā ca nāmoktyā
tapaḥ pūjākriyādiṣu
nyūnaṁ saṁpūrṇatāṁ yāti
sadyo vande tam acyutaṁ

mantrahīnaṁ kriyāhīnaṁ bhaktihīnaṁ ramāpate
yatkṛtaṁ tu mayā deva paripūrṇaṁ tad astu me

lines.meaning: By remembrance of whom and by utterance of whose name—

words.meaning: by utterance of the name (nāma + ukti)

lines.meaning: In austerities, acts of worship, and the like—

words.meaning: in worship rites and the like (pūjā + kriyā + ādi)

lines.meaning: What is deficient becomes complete.
I bow to that Acyuta, who makes this happen at once.
O Lord of Ramā, [this worship is] deficient in mantra, action, and devotion.

lines.text: yatkṛtaṁ tu mayā deva paripūrṇaṁ tad astu me
lines.meaning: O Lord, may what I have done become fully complete for me.

readingNotes: Preserves the printed yatkṛtaṁ ... tad astu me. It does not substitute yatpūjanaṁ or tad astu te from other versions.
tapaḥ is printed separately before pūjākriyādiṣu; the intended collective sense is “in austerity, worship rites, and so on,” but the printed nominal construction is retained.
sadyaḥ appears as sadyo before vande by sandhi.

samarpana.text:
anena vāhanapūjākaraṇena
asmadgurvantargata bhāratīramaṇa mukhyaprāṇāntargata
śrī durgāsahita śrī lakṣmīnārāyaṇa prīyatāṁ

kṛṣṇārpaṇam astu

lines.meaning: By this performance of vehicle worship—

words.meaning: by performing vehicle worship (vāhana + pūjā + karaṇa)

lines.meaning: [The Lord] indwelling our guru and indwelling Mukhyaprāṇa, the husband of Bhāratī—

words.meaning: indwelling our guru (asmad + guru + antargata); the printed source has an extra u before v; the display uses regular guru + antargata sandhi
husband of Bhāratī (Bhāratī + ramaṇa), qualifying Mukhyaprāṇa
indwelling Mukhyaprāṇa (mukhya, chief + prāṇa, vital breath + antargata)

lines.meaning: May Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa, accompanied by Śrī Durgā, be pleased.
May this be an offering to Kṛṣṇa.

readingNotes: The source says vāhana (vehicle) here; it is not silently changed to āyudha (implement).
The indwelling chain is preserved as an uninflected source sequence; it is interpreted in the source’s Mādhva context, not expanded into a new hierarchy.

The printed asmadguruvantargata has been normalized to asmadgurvantargata by the regular guru + antargata vowel sandhi. This is explicitly a proposed grammatical normalization; confirm the intended recitation.

corrections.reason: Proposed normalization of guru + antargata to gurvantargata; removes the extra printed u before v.
Separates arpaṇam and astu for learning without changing the recited sounds.
